title: Average order value by customer segment
prompt: Are wholesale customers placing bigger orders than retail customers, on average? Compare average order value (after discounts) by customer segment.
population: All orders with at least one order item, joined to their customer's segment.
metricDefinition: average, per order, of sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) across its order_items, grouped by customer segment.
referenceSql: SELECT c.segment, avg(order_totals.total) AS avg_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) AS total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) order_totals ON order_totals.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.segment

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT c.segment, avg(oi.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.segment
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Averages line-item unit price directly, ignoring quantity and discount and mixing the order_items grain into a per-order metric — a classic grain mistake.
